explanation: The two remote claims are CONFIRMED as current replay-18.7.0 protection gaps, not new 18.10.0 regressions: the entitlement bypass is a strong source inference, while the effective-API catch loss also has parent-executed compact() evidence in research/compact-effective-lane-probe.json (one intercepted V1 request containing synthetic history). Configured host next-method fallback is intentional and distinct from both hidden internal replays; successful-compaction metadata/baseline commit is correctly deferred until collector acceptance, and neither connection ownership nor that commit protocol prevents the entitlement replay. The relevant local-compaction migration claim is QUALIFIED as a real request-shape capability loss, not demonstrated server cache loss (B compaction.ts:1044–1076 and 2547–2605 versus T:890–925 and 1980–2009); target already uses host-rendered native context, but only for the cut prefix, and image accounting cannot neutralize either text-only remote counterexample—no additional image/snapcompact verdict is asserted outside that boundary, no reviewer executions or edits occurred, and all three required policy greps matched.

findings.title: Block entitlement-rejection SSE replay in the chain-only compaction lane
findings.body: CONFIRMED, CURRENT-BASELINE protection gap; source inference, not an executed local-WS observation. The added transport-exception guard is bypassed by the buffered-error dispatch at openai-codex-responses.ts:1962–1976, which directly calls openCodexSseTransport. This is reachable with a model/account advertising daybreak_blue, a synthetic OAuth-shaped token identifying that account, and a completed ordinary WS turn on the same providerSessionState/session/model/backend/account and non-Lite connection: createCodexRequestContext:1472–1473 applies access_programs, access-programs.ts:47–59 recognizes invalid_access_program and strips it, and streamRequest:4818–4831 yields an idless error frame and terminates normally rather than throwing into the guarded catch. No request option intercepts the direct replay; openCodexSseTransport:2311–2354 sends the complete transformed body without previous_response_id. Connection busy ownership is released at streamRequest:4833–4843 before replay. If SSE subsequently returns valid compaction output, compaction-v2-streaming.ts:446–474 accepts it and invokes the normal metadata commit/baseline reset; deferred commit therefore does not enforce transport policy, and the returned diagnostics can still describe the original WS send. This is not the host's explicitly configured next-method fallback at session-maintenance.ts:1529–1550 or 5212–5232. Minimal fix: reject compaction-wire bodies before any SSE open, including this entitlement branch, with a typed chain-loss failure while preserving ordinary-turn entitlement recovery; any recovery must return through validated WS chaining. Narrow parent probe: use the actual requestCompactionV2Streaming consumer against a local WS server, establish a successful ordinary-turn baseline, then emit invalid_access_program only for the chained compaction frame; intercept/count HTTP requests and require zero, plus no successful compaction result from that rejected attempt. Use a fresh synthetic account/model key so the process-local droppedPrograms set does not suppress the trigger. No real entitlement or provider cache behavior is needed to establish this client-side replay.

findings.title: Preserve chain-loss errors for the effective Codex compaction API
findings.body: CONFIRMED, CURRENT-BASELINE defect, independently source-traced and reproduced by the parent at the actual compact() consumer. With model.api=openai-responses, provider=openai, remoteCompaction.api=openai-codex-responses, v2StreamingEnabled=true, enabled=true, a compatible V1 endpoint and nonempty fitting history, compact():2149–2153 admits V2; compaction-v2-streaming.ts:153–175 recognizes the effective Codex lane but rejects its unavailable live provider transport with CodexCompactionChainLostError at 303–305. The new catch tests native model.api through isCodexResponsesModel instead, so it swallows that sentinel and enters V1 at compact():2380. openai.ts:342–356 explicitly admits this configuration, and requestOpenAiRemoteCompaction:806–912 has no chain-loss guard before its full-history POST. Host candidate eligibility is not a blanket prohibition: session-maintenance.ts:163–172 permits same-provider non-Anthropic candidates when native compaction is enabled, and direct compact() is itself the affected exported consumer. The parent artifact research/compact-effective-lane-probe.json records forbiddenRequestCount=1 and the synthetic user history in the intercepted /responses/compact body; its fetch abort prevented real network activity, so successful V1 output is neither claimed nor needed. Minimal fix: unconditionally rethrow CodexCompactionChainLostError and use isCodexCompactionV2Lane for the outer no-V1 policy, retaining native model.api checks only where serializer typing requires them. Preserve the host's explicit, noticed next-method fallback rather than banning it. The existing parent probe is the narrow discriminating reproduction; after a fix, that same actual compact() invocation should surface the chain-loss sentinel with zero fetch calls, without adding a lower-level mock or another redundant probe.
